note: Gold articles are the ones a correct answer must cite, decided when the question was written. Seeds (status kept) were chosen by Tianyi on 2026-11-13; drafts await his review. Frozen only after review. Cut to 30 on 2026-11-17 (D-024); the rest are in gold_reserve.json.

questions.question: My car is leased through Harbor. Can I sell it to you?
questions.perfect_answer: Not directly. Harbor Leasing doesn't allow third-party buyouts, so Northwind can't buy the car from them. You could buy it out yourself first, or return it at the end of the lease.
questions.what_makes_it_hard: 'Harbor' matches Harbor Leasing (a leasing company) and Harbor Trust Bank (a lender); 'leased' is the only clue. Embeddings can't tell company names apart.
questions.author: claude

questions.question: Which form do I sign so you can get the payoff number, NW-LPA-1 or NW-LSE-1? It's a lease.
questions.perfect_answer: NW-LSE-1. It's the lease buyout authorization, which lets Northwind request the dealer payoff quote from your leasing company. NW-LPA-1 is for loans.
questions.what_makes_it_hard: The two codes differ by two letters and both 'let Northwind get a payoff number'. text_en splits codes into tokens and embeddings blur them; lease vs. loan is the only real difference.
questions.author: claude

questions.question: What's form NW-LRL-1 for?
questions.perfect_answer: It's the lien release request. If your loan is paid off but the title still lists the lender, sign NW-LRL-1 and Northwind contacts the lender for the release; it can add 1 to 2 weeks.
questions.what_makes_it_hard: The question is only a code. Other lender-related forms (NW-LPA-1 in the payoff-letter article) look close to an embedding.
questions.author: claude
questions.why_in_30: A bare form code: tests the exact-match `codes` field (I-002). The payoff-letter article is a look-alike trap.

questions.question: The bank still has the pink slip because I haven't finished paying the car off. Can I still sell it to you?
questions.perfect_answer: Yes. While a loan is open, your lender holds the title. Northwind pays the lender off from your offer, so you don't need the title in hand.
questions.what_makes_it_hard: 'Pink slip' and 'bank' share no words with 'title' and 'lienholder'; the lost-title article ('we cannot buy without a title') looks closest.
questions.author: claude

questions.question: My father passed away in March and the car is still in his name. I'd like to sell it.
questions.perfect_answer: You can sell it as his heir or the executor. Bring the death certificate and either the court letters or, for a small estate, affidavit NW-EST-1.
questions.what_makes_it_hard: No 'inherit', 'heir' or 'estate' in the question. The family-car article looks like a perfect match but needs a power of attorney, which ends when the person dies.
questions.author: claude

questions.question: Do I need to get rid of my stuff in the car's computer before you take it?
questions.perfect_answer: Yes. Unpair your phone, clear garage door codes, remove toll tags, and remove the car from any connected-car app.
questions.what_makes_it_hard: 'Stuff in the car's computer' never says phone, toll tag or data.
questions.author: claude
questions.why_in_30: Shares almost no words with its article ('stuff in the car's computer' = personal data, paired phones): the purest paraphrase test.

questions.question: I still have a loan with Bayline Credit Union. Do I need to get a payoff letter before I come in?
questions.perfect_answer: No. Bayline is in Northwind's e-payoff network, so Northwind confirms the payoff with them directly the same day, with no letter needed.
questions.what_makes_it_hard: The payoff-letter article is the closest match and says to bring a letter. The exception lives in the lender record (Bayline is in the network) and the e-payoff article.
questions.author: claude

questions.question: I lease from Crescent and your offer is higher than my buyout. Do I get the extra money?
questions.perfect_answer: Yes. Since February 1, 2026 Crescent allows third-party buyouts, and Crescent passes the difference to you.
questions.what_makes_it_hard: Two articles (which lessors allow buyouts; who keeps the equity), and the 2022 buyout article says Crescent doesn't allow it.
questions.author: claude

questions.question: my lein holder is harbor, they said call u guys for the payof number
questions.perfect_answer: Harbor Trust Bank isn't in Northwind's e-payoff network, so a 15-day payoff letter is needed. You can request it yourself, or sign NW-LPA-1 and Northwind requests it for you.
questions.what_makes_it_hard: Two typos ('lein', 'payof') and an ambiguous 'harbor'. 'Lienholder' means a loan, so it's Harbor Trust Bank, not Harbor Leasing.
questions.author: claude

questions.question: I'm using home pickup and I still owe Pinewood Federal. When does Pinewood get paid, and is anything taken out of what I get?
questions.perfect_answer: Pinewood Federal Credit Union is in the e-payoff network, so it's paid the same day. You get the offer minus the payoff, minus the $99 home pickup fee.
questions.what_makes_it_hard: Three facts in three articles: the fee (home pickup), the payment timing (getting paid) and whether Pinewood is a network lender (e-payoff).
questions.author: claude
questions.why_in_30: Needs three articles (home pickup, getting paid, e-payoff network); only the first looks like the question. The lender name is the bridge.

questions.question: My offer expired while I was waiting for a duplicate title from North Carolina. Do I have to start over, and will the price be the same?
questions.perfect_answer: Yes, request a new offer; the amount reflects current market prices and may be higher or lower. North Carolina duplicates take 4 to 6 weeks, so book the appointment for when it arrives.
questions.what_makes_it_hard: The duplicate-title article only says you 'may need a new one'; what happens to the price is in the offer article.
questions.author: claude
questions.why_in_30: A state article (duplicate title in North Carolina) plus the offer-validity article; the price answer is only in the second.

questions.question: I bought my car from you with a loan from Bayline Credit Union. Now I want to sell it back before it's paid off. Who has my title, and do I need a payoff letter?
questions.perfect_answer: Bayline holds the title until the loan is paid off. You can still sell: Northwind pays Bayline from your offer, and because Bayline is in the e-payoff network, no payoff letter is needed.
questions.what_makes_it_hard: It starts on the buying side and ends on the selling side. The Northwind-financing title article looks closer but is the wrong lender.
questions.author: claude
questions.why_in_30: Starts on the buying side and ends on the selling side, with a trap that looks closer (Northwind-financed titles).

questions.question: My dad passed away and his car is still financed with Lakeshore Bank. Do I need a payoff letter to sell it?
questions.perfect_answer: No payoff letter: Lakeshore Bank is in the e-payoff network. You still need the death certificate plus court letters or NW-EST-1, and Northwind pays the loan off from the offer.
questions.what_makes_it_hard: Inherited → loan → network lender: three hops, and the family-car article (power of attorney) is a confident wrong turn.
questions.author: claude
questions.why_in_30: Inheritance + loan + e-payoff network; the lender name is the only path to the third article.

questions.question: I got my offer on January 28 and I can't come in until February 4. The website says offers last 5 days. Did mine expire?
questions.perfect_answer: No. Offers issued before February 1, 2026 keep the old 7-day terms, so yours is good through February 4.
questions.what_makes_it_hard: The 2026 headline rule says it expired; only the transition clause inside the 2026 article gives the right answer, so filtering to current versions isn't enough.
questions.author: claude

questions.question: My mom signed the old notarized power of attorney for me back in January. My appointment is July 10. Can I still use it?
questions.perfect_answer: No. NW-POA-1 forms signed before February 1 are accepted only until June 30, 2026. She needs to sign NW-POA-2, which can be signed electronically.
questions.what_makes_it_hard: The code is never said ('the old notarized one' = NW-POA-1), the deadline falls between the question and the appointment, and an unchanged article still cites NW-POA-1 as current.
questions.author: claude

questions.question: Back in December 2025 I got an offer. How many miles could I put on the car before it expired?
questions.perfect_answer: 300 miles, or 7 days, whichever came first. That was the rule until January 31, 2026.
questions.what_makes_it_hard: The question is about the past: the current 2026 version (250 miles) is the trap here, and filtering to 'today' picks it.
questions.author: claude
questions.why_in_30: About December 2025, so the 2022 version is right; a method that filters on 'today' instead of as_of fails on purpose (D-019).

questions.question: Is Granite Bank in your e-payoff network? My appointment is next week.
questions.perfect_answer: Not yet: Granite Bank joins on March 15, 2026. For next week's appointment, bring a payoff letter or sign NW-LPA-1 so Northwind requests one.
questions.what_makes_it_hard: The article lists Granite next to the network lenders; the joining date is the whole answer.
questions.author: claude
questions.why_in_30: The answer is a lender's joining date in the e-payoff network, checked against the appointment date.

questions.question: Can you mail me a check for my car like you did for my friend in 2023?
questions.perfect_answer: Not anymore. Northwind stopped mailing checks on February 1, 2026; you get a bank draft or a direct deposit (1 to 3 business days).
questions.what_makes_it_hard: The friend's 2023 story matches the 2022 version, which offered mailed checks.
questions.author: claude
questions.why_in_30: The friend's 2023 mailed check matches the old version: the 'agent repeats an outdated answer' case this cookbook is about.

questions.question: I live in Georgia. My brother co-owns the car but he's deployed overseas with the Army. Does his power of attorney have to be notarized?
questions.perfect_answer: No. A deployed owner can sign NW-MIL-1, which replaces a notarized power of attorney in every state, including Georgia.
questions.what_makes_it_hard: The co-owners article says Georgia always requires a notary, the obvious and wrong answer here: an exception to an exception.
questions.author: claude

questions.question: I moved from California to North Carolina last year, but the car is still registered in California. What do I do with the plates when I sell?
questions.perfect_answer: Plates follow the state that issued them. They're California plates, so return them to California within 10 days and keep the NW-PLT-1 receipt.
questions.what_makes_it_hard: Two states in one question. North Carolina's rule (plates stay on the car) matches where the customer lives, and it's the wrong one.
questions.author: claude

questions.question: Since you guys won't buy a car unless I have the title in my hand, I guess I have to pay off my whole loan first?
questions.perfect_answer: No. You don't need the title or to pay the loan off first. Your lender holds the title, and Northwind pays the lender from your offer.
questions.what_makes_it_hard: A false premise. The lost-title article seems to confirm it ('we cannot buy ... without a title'), and bots tend to agree with the user.
questions.author: claude

questions.question: I live in Texas. Can someone come pick up my car?
questions.perfect_answer: Not in Texas: home pickup isn't available there, so bring the car to a store.
questions.what_makes_it_hard: The 2022 version says pickup is available in every state.
questions.author: claude
questions.why_in_30: The 2022 version says pickup works in every state; the current one excludes Texas.

questions.question: I inherited my uncle's car in North Carolina. There's still a loan on it and nobody can find the title. What do I need to bring to sell it?
questions.perfect_answer: You don't need the title: the lender holds it while the loan is open. Bring your photo ID, the death certificate, court letters or NW-EST-1 for a small estate, a 15-day payoff letter (not needed if the lender is in the e-payoff network), a current registration (North Carolina requires it), all keys, and NW-ODO-2.
questions.what_makes_it_hard: The lost-title and North Carolina duplicate-title articles look most relevant and would send the customer on a 4 to 6 week detour that isn't needed. The real items are spread across five articles.
questions.author: claude

questions.question: I want to sell my leased car using home pickup. I'm in Texas. What do I need to have ready?
questions.perfect_answer: Home pickup isn't available in Texas, so you'll need to bring the car to a store. Bring your photo ID, the registration, all keys, the dealer payoff quote from your leasing company (or sign NW-LSE-1 so Northwind requests it), and NW-ODO-2.
questions.what_makes_it_hard: The checklist rests on a premise that's false in this state; a bot that just collects requirements lists NW-PU-1 and pickup steps.
questions.author: claude

questions.question: My car is paid off but I lost the title, and I'm in California. Walk me through everything I need to do to sell it.
questions.perfect_answer: Get a duplicate title at a California motor vehicle office (same day at the main offices, 2 to 3 weeks by mail); you can get an offer and book meanwhile. Bring your photo ID, the registration, all keys, the duplicate title and NW-ODO-2. After the sale, return the plates to California within 10 days with the NW-PLT-1 receipt.
questions.what_makes_it_hard: Four articles, and the plate rule is easy to forget because it applies after the sale.
questions.author: claude
questions.why_in_30: Four articles across titles, a state's duplicate-title process and plates: the list is spread out.

questions.question: I owe more on my car than your offer, and my loan is with Coastal Credit Union. What do I bring to finish the sale?
questions.perfect_answer: A 15-day payoff letter from Coastal (it isn't in the e-payoff network; or sign NW-LPA-1 so Northwind requests it), plus a cashier's check or debit card for the difference, your photo ID, the registration, all keys and NW-ODO-2.
questions.what_makes_it_hard: Whether Coastal needs a letter depends on the network list, and the 2022 version still allows personal checks.
questions.author: claude
questions.why_in_30: Negative equity, payoff letter, e-payoff network and the appointment checklist: four articles from one lender name.

questions.question: Before I hand my car over to you, what should I do about my insurance, plates, toll tag and all that? I'm in North Carolina.
questions.perfect_answer: Keep the car insured until the sale is complete, then cancel. Leave the plates on the car (in North Carolina, plates stay with the vehicle). Remove the toll tag, clear garage codes and unpair your phone.
questions.what_makes_it_hard: The 2022 plates article says always remove them, and three small topics live in three articles.
questions.author: claude
questions.why_in_30: Insurance, plates and toll tags: three articles that look unrelated, plus a state rule.

questions.question: Can you buy my car if it's registered in Canada?
questions.perfect_answer: The help center doesn't cover cars registered outside the country; please contact a store.
questions.what_makes_it_hard: 'Selling a car registered in another state' is a very close match, and a bot will happily apply state rules to another country.
questions.author: claude

questions.question: My car has an open recall and an open insurance claim from a hailstorm. Will you still buy it?
questions.perfect_answer: The open recall isn't a problem: Northwind still buys cars with open recalls. The help center doesn't cover open insurance claims, so please ask a store about that part.
questions.what_makes_it_hard: Half of it is answerable; bots tend to answer everything from the half they found, or refuse everything.
questions.author: claude

questions.question: What interest rate would I get if I finance my next car with Northwind Auto Finance?
questions.perfect_answer: The help center doesn't cover financing rates or credit checks; please ask a store or Northwind Auto Finance.
questions.what_makes_it_hard: The Northwind-financing title article names Northwind Auto Finance, so it looks like the place to answer from.
questions.author: claude
questions.why_in_30: The Northwind-financing article looks like the place to answer from, but the KB never gives rates: should refuse.
